case_name: Meridian Retail Group — Supplier Invoice Dispute Transformation

executive_summary.statement: Meridian's dispute process is a multi-system exception workflow in which AP analysts must reconstruct facts from SAP, Coupa, Outlook, SharePoint, receiving/logistics records, and supplier-specific commercial terms before determining a disposition.
Historical performance is weak relative to stated service levels: the analyzed dataset shows 62% SLA attainment, 6.8 business days average resolution time, and a 14% reopen rate.
Missing evidence is strongly associated with poorer operating outcomes: cases marked as missing evidence achieved 13.3% SLA attainment versus 68.6% without missing evidence.

Supplier-specific terms materially change otherwise standard AP decisions, creating a recurring need to identify the correct governing document before resolving price, freight, dispute-window, quantity, and service cases.
A material part of operational complexity appears to arise from evidence retrieval, interpretation, and handoffs rather than from the arithmetic of invoice matching alone.

process_steps.trigger: Invoice enters Meridian AP processing and fails standard automated validation.
process_steps.activity: Create an invoice exception and assign a reason code when sufficient information is available.
process_steps.decision_required: Whether the invoice can process automatically or requires exception handling.
policy_constraints: Reason code must be validated by the assigned analyst.

process_steps.activity: Verify the actual issue and assemble the factual and commercial evidence needed to resolve it.
process_steps.decision_required: Whether available evidence is sufficient and which additional sources or stakeholders are required.
policy_constraints: Analyst should avoid requesting evidence already available internally.
Supplier-specific executed terms can override generic policy.

process_steps.activity: Determine the cause of the discrepancy and identify the commercial or procedural rule that governs the case.
process_steps.decision_required: Which policy or supplier-specific term governs and whether the case is sufficiently clear to resolve.
policy_constraints: Informal email and historical treatment are not automatically authoritative.
process_steps.approval_required: Specialist review where policy requires it.
failure_modes: Reliance on precedent without validating current terms

process_steps.trigger: Evidence is incomplete, authority is insufficient, or interpretation is ambiguous.
process_steps.activity: Request missing information or route the case to the function with authority to resolve the ambiguity.
process_steps.decision_required: Who owns the unresolved question and whether the case should remain pending or be escalated.
policy_constraints: Cases awaiting evidence remain PENDING INFORMATION.
Escalation should state the evidence and specific decision required.
process_steps.approval_required: Depends on subject matter and disputed amount.
failure_modes: Escalation because a case is time-consuming rather than truly ambiguous

process_steps.trigger: Evidence and governing rule are sufficient to make a disposition.
process_steps.activity: Select the resolution disposition and obtain required approval according to disputed amount and policy.
process_steps.decision_required: PAY_AS_INVOICED, PAY_PO_AMOUNT, PARTIAL_ADJUSTMENT, REQUEST_CREDIT_NOTE, REJECT_DISPUTE, or ESCALATE.
policy_constraints: Approval authority is based on original disputed amount.
Certain strategic-supplier situations require Procurement consultation.
process_steps.approval_required: < $10k analyst; $10k–$50k team lead; $50k–$250k AP manager; > $250k Finance Director.

process_steps.process_step: System update, supplier communication, and closure
process_steps.activity: Update the system of record, enter case notes, communicate the outcome to the supplier when required, and close the dispute.
process_steps.decision_required: What information must be recorded and communicated externally.
policy_constraints: Case notes must be sufficient for another qualified employee to understand the decision.
Supplier communication must not disclose inappropriate internal information.
process_steps.approval_required: Resolution approval must already be complete.

process_steps.trigger: Periodic quality review, new supplier evidence, internal challenge, or discovered processing error.
process_steps.activity: Assess decision accuracy, documentation, approvals, and communications; reopen if warranted.
process_steps.decision_required: Whether the closed resolution remains supportable.
policy_constraints: Reason for reopening must be documented.
failure_modes: Inability to reconstruct prior decision from weak notes

diagnostic_findings.finding: Evidence fragmentation is a central operating constraint: analysts are expected to assemble case facts from multiple systems and repositories before deciding a dispute.
support: SOP names SAP, Coupa, Outlook, SharePoint, and TMS as required sources depending on case type.
Supplier-specific agreements and selected case packets show that a single decision can depend on multiple documents and operational records.
diagnostic_findings.operational_impact: Creates search effort, context switching, and dependence on complete/correct evidence before resolution can proceed.

diagnostic_findings.finding: Missing evidence is associated with a major deterioration in SLA performance.
support: Missing-evidence cases achieved 13.3% SLA attainment versus 68.6% when evidence was not missing.
Average resolution time is 14.4 days with missing evidence versus 5.8 days without it.
diagnostic_findings.operational_impact: Cases lacking evidence are disproportionately likely to miss service targets and remain open longer.

diagnostic_findings.finding: Supplier-specific terms create decision complexity that cannot be safely resolved using generic policy alone.
support: NorthStar changes standard dispute windows, freight terms, and promotional pricing logic.
Apex introduces quantity tolerances and mixed materials/services treatment.
Solara contains time-limited freight amendments and an unresolved continuation trail.
diagnostic_findings.operational_impact: Analysts must locate and correctly sequence supplier-specific agreements before applying standard rules.

diagnostic_findings.finding: Historical treatment is an unreliable substitute for current authoritative evidence.
support: Generic policy explicitly warns that prior cases may be outdated, erroneous, or one-time exceptions.
A selected contract case contains prior notes such as 'approved per buyer' and 'exception — pay this time only' that do not establish governing terms.
diagnostic_findings.operational_impact: Weak precedent can propagate inconsistent or unsupported decisions and reduce auditability.

diagnostic_findings.finding: Reopened disputes represent substantial rework rather than a minor administrative event.
support: Reopened cases average 40.2 handling minutes versus 21.3 for non-reopened cases.
Reopened cases average 10.2 resolution days versus 6.3 otherwise.
diagnostic_findings.operational_impact: Reopening consumes additional analyst capacity and extends end-to-end cycle time.

diagnostic_findings.finding: Some disputes are composite cases that require component-level treatment rather than a single invoice-level binary decision.
support: Apex agreement requires materials and installation portions of mixed invoices to be validated independently.
A selected Apex case contains valid materials and labor but unsupported freight.
diagnostic_findings.operational_impact: A simplistic resolve/reject workflow can hold valid amounts unnecessarily or produce incorrect whole-invoice decisions.

diagnostic_findings.finding: The current operating model relies heavily on analysts to recognize when ambiguity requires specialist authority rather than individual interpretation.
support: SOP and policy require escalation to Procurement, Tax, Receiving, or Logistics under different ambiguity conditions.
Solara freight and tax examples cannot be resolved safely by AP alone.
diagnostic_findings.operational_impact: Outcome quality depends on analyst judgment about when to resolve versus escalate, creating potential variation across employees.

source_conflicts.description: Solara's executed freight amendments expire at December 31, 2025, while a Procurement email states that the existing setup should continue into 2026 and an unsigned draft proposes formal 2026 terms.
source_conflicts.why_unresolved: Meridian policy states that informal email does not ordinarily override executed commercial documentation, and the proposed Amendment 3 is explicitly unexecuted.
source_conflicts.required_authority: Procurement / Legal confirmation of the governing 2026 freight terms.

diagnostic_hypotheses.hypothesis: Evidence retrieval and completeness are likely meaningful drivers of end-to-end delay in the dispute process.
basis: Missing-evidence cases show 13.3% SLA attainment versus 68.6% without missing evidence.
The SOP requires analysts to retrieve evidence from several repositories and functions.
how_to_test: Measure active search/retrieval time separately from decision time.
Track time spent in PENDING INFORMATION by reason code and supplier.
Instrument repository/system access sequence for a representative sample.

diagnostic_hypotheses.hypothesis: Policy and contract interpretation likely explain a disproportionate share of high-complexity cases even if they are not the largest volume category.
basis: Supplier-specific agreements contain multiple overrides and ambiguity patterns.
Contract disputes require document precedence and specialist escalation when terms conflict.
how_to_test: Compare handling time and SLA by confirmed root cause, not only intake reason code.
Measure document count and escalation rate for contract-related cases.
Review a sample of reopened cases for contract/policy interpretation errors.

diagnostic_hypotheses.hypothesis: Variation in analyst outcomes may partly reflect inconsistent access to institutional knowledge and escalation judgment rather than individual productivity alone.
basis: Policies require judgment about when to escalate.
The process depends on supplier-specific and context-specific rules.
how_to_test: Compare analysts after controlling for case mix and supplier.
Review escalation decisions for similar case archetypes.
Interview analysts regarding undocumented supplier-specific knowledge.

limitations: The historical client-facing dataset does not contain authoritative actual-root-cause labels, so intake reason-code accuracy cannot be independently validated in this diagnosis.
Historical resolution outcomes are observations, not proof that the underlying decision was correct.
The dataset is a 250-case synthetic sample rather than the full 180,000-case annual population.
Resolution-days data combines internal work and waiting time; it does not isolate active processing from external dependencies.
The current dataset does not contain a direct measure of search time, queue time, or time spent in PENDING INFORMATION.
No employee interviews or system telemetry are included in the current source pack.
